identification: Two rough-sawn Tasmanian Huon pine slabs (pale yellow, dark pin flecks), roughly 1.5 to 2.3 m long. One narrow live-edge slab has a large void/branch fork near the base; the other is a straighter, narrow, clean slab. Likely slabs sawn from salvage or offcuts, not wide boards.

viewing_check: Measure both slabs (length, width, thickness). Check the void slab for cracks or rot/stain depth, and confirm both are genuine Huon pine (scent, pin flecks), not celery top or white-pine look-alikes. Check for splits through the wider face.
